# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree

# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,

  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: false

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 696
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/696
- **Title**: chore(pin): awf workflows → fd84ab19 (kicker real ticks + per-SHA concurrency)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `pin/awf-kicker-fd84ab19` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +5
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:00:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:17Z

## PR Description

Mechanical re-pin of the factory-workflow immutable SHA `e611e5f4` → `fd84ab19`. Brings two awf fixes:

- **awf #13** — kicker dispatches REAL ticks: a bare `gh workflow run` lands dryRun=true; the kicker now passes `-F dryRun=false`.
- **awf #14** — per-head-SHA concurrency: queued kickers are no longer superseded by every push (a pending run in a shared group is ALWAYS displaced — `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING one). Required contexts (`sm-liveness`/`head-completeness`) stop dying CANCELLED on fresh heads. Root cause of dmtools-agents #682 (live: fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03; eight branches cancelled in one 36s dev-wave 06:21–06:22 2026-10-04).

Refs: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#13, #14 · IstiN/dmtools-agents#682 (+ standing remedy in dmtools-agents#695).

Note: if your kicker stub declares its OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too — a caller-level global group re-introduces the supersession locally (dmtools-agents scoped its stub in #695; fa/dart stubs declare none).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

{"body":"Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). # Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      # Docs-only CI is the repo's PR check (workflow_run fallback name).
      ci_workflow: agent-docs.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. - **Title**: chore(pin): awf workflows → fd84ab19 (kicker real ticks + per-SHA concurrency)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `pin/awf-kicker-fd84ab19` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +5
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:00:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:17Z

## PR Description

Mechanical re-pin of the factory-workflow immutable SHA `e611e5f4` → `fd84ab19`. Brings two awf fixes:

- **awf #13** — kicker dispatches REAL ticks: a bare `gh workflow run` lands dryRun=true; the kicker now passes `-F dryRun=false`.
- **awf #14** — per-head-SHA concurrency: queued kickers are no longer superseded by every push (a pending run in a shared group is ALWAYS displaced — `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING one). Required contexts (`sm-liveness`/`head-completeness`) stop dying CANCELLED on fresh heads. Root cause of dmtools-agents #682 (live: fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03; eight branches cancelled in one 36s dev-wave 06:21–06:22 2026-10-04).

Refs: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#13, #14 · IstiN/dmtools-agents#682 (+ standing remedy in dmtools-agents#695).

Note: if your kicker stub declares its OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too — a caller-level global group re-introduces the supersession locally (dmtools-agents scoped its stub in #695; fa/dart stubs declare none).

messages.preview: The PR description claims a re-pin to immutable SHA `fd84ab19`, but the diff actually pins to `@main`. Let me verify the full context of the changed files and repo conventions.

blocks.text:
This is a critical finding. The PR description says:

> Mechanical re-pin of the factory-workflow immutable SHA `e611e5f4` → `fd84ab19`.

But the actual diff pins the workflows to `@main` — NOT to the immutable SHA `fd84ab19`! That's a major mismatch:

1. The PR claims to re-pin to the immutable SHA `fd84ab19`, but the diff actually changes pins to `@main` (mutable branch reference).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

{"body":"Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      # Docs-only CI is the repo's PR check (workflow_run fallback name).
      ci_workflow: agent-docs.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.

# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —

name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed
    secrets: inherit

- **Title**: chore(pin): awf workflows → fd84ab19 (kicker real ticks + per-SHA concurrency)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `pin/awf-kicker-fd84ab19` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +5
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:00:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T07:54:17Z

## PR Description

Mechanical re-pin of the factory-workflow immutable SHA `e611e5f4` → `fd84ab19`. Brings two awf fixes:

- **awf #13** — kicker dispatches REAL ticks: a bare `gh workflow run` lands dryRun=true; the kicker now passes `-F dryRun=false`.
- **awf #14** — per-head-SHA concurrency: queued kickers are no longer superseded by every push (a pending run in a shared group is ALWAYS displaced — `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING one). Required contexts (`sm-liveness`/`head-completeness`) stop dying CANCELLED on fresh heads. Root cause of dmtools-agents #682 (live: fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03; eight branches cancelled in one 36s dev-wave 06:21–06:22 2026-10-04).

Refs: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows#13, #14 · IstiN/dmtools-agents#682 (+ standing remedy in dmtools-agents#695).

Note: if your kicker stub declares its OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too — a caller-level global group re-introduces the supersession locally (dmtools-agents scoped its stub in #695; fa/dart stubs declare none).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.

{"body":"Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

Now the bigger question — the title/description mismatch:

PR title: "chore(pin): awf workflows → fd84ab19 (kicker real ticks + per-SHA concurrency)".

name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:

    types: [completed]
  pull_request:

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),

# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration

# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must

  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:

    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

{"body":"Closes #682 (PR 1 of 2 — the kicker-side fix lands in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; this PR is the standing SM remedy + this repo's own stub scoping).

## Evidence (#682)

- **fa#1202** (head `898efd4`): all 4 kicker push-runs on `ai/gh-1171` CANCELLED 21:43–23:05 as silent-refresh pushes landed; required checks ended CANCELLED → PR BLOCKED until the manual rerun at 23:26.
- **fa#1203**: same pattern twice (23:47, 23:57) — the queue head stalled on it.
- **Still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22**: eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave (fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010); this repo's own kicker showed the same at 06:36/06:41/06:43.
- Cost on 2026-10-03 alone: 2 dead zones on queue heads + 2 manual reruns.

Mechanism: a queued run in a shared concurrency group **always supersedes the pending one** — *"Any existing pending job or workflow in the same concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place"* (GitHub docs). `cancel-in-progress: false` only shields the RUNNING run. Every silent-refresh push therefore killed the pending kicker, and no rule treated CANCELLED as re-runnable (the #632 class, now triggered by our own refresh machinery).

## What this PR does

**1. Standing rule `rerun-cancelled-checks`** (`sm_github.json`, FIRST in the array):

- match: armed (`ai_validating`) or latched (`ai_validated`) PR; not BEHIND (silent-update refreshes that head), not DIRTY (conflict-rework owns it), not `agent:rework`;
- `localAction rerun_cancelled_checks` (js/smAgent.js):
  - scans the head's check runs — only contexts that currently read **CANCELLED** among `rule.requiredContexts` act (dart: `static`/`gate`/`agents-gate`; fa: the kicker's `kicker / sm-liveness`, `kicker / head-completeness`). Failure paths untouched — red stays `fail_validation` territory;
  - once-per-head marker comment (conflict_rework pacing) citing fa#1202/#1203 + 2026-10-04 06:21, posted AFTER the reruns land (the gh-683 bug C invariant: a failed rerun posts no marker, the next tick retries);
  - **no in-flight run on the head** guard — the `hasActiveDispatchedRun` probe pattern widened to every run on the head (any event): an active run re-stamps the contexts by itself;
  - `gh run rerun <id>` of the latest **attempt-1** cancelled run per required context (deduped per run id); a run already re-run and still cancelled is skipped — no automatic retry loop.
- Placement: it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, so it **cannot fight `sweep-stale-validating`** (cancelled conclusions never sweep by design anyway); the documented #637 invariant (merge-validated before sweep) is preserved by prefixing, never interleaving.

**2. This repo's own kicker stub** (`.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml`): the caller-level global `sm-kicker` group alone would keep superseding pending kickers even after the canonical awf fix is re-pinned — scoped to `sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}` (effective once the pin bump lands; pin bumps are separate PRs by repo convention).

## Tests

10 new unit tests in the existing `test_smAgent.js` rule-test patterns (rerun+marker shape, rerun-failure posts no marker, CANCELLED-only matching, in-flight skip, once-per-head pacing, attempt-2 no-loop, newest-run-wins, dry-run, no-config skip, and a `sm_github.json` placement pin asserting rule order). Node harness: 178 passed, 1 failed — the single failure is the pre-existing `assert.doesNotThrow` mock gap present on clean `main` (the canonical gate is the pack-release test job). `actionlint` clean. #684/#685/#686 suites untouched and green.

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (frozen machine loop).
#
# Same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: pinned immutable SHA of
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows; agents/CLI resolve from releases by
# vars.AGENTS_VERSION / vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION.
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Agent Docs']   # the only per-PR check this repo dispatches
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (same pin as machine-sm.yml — bump both together).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@main
    with:
      # Docs-only CI is the repo's PR check (workflow_run fallback name).
      ci_workflow: agent-docs.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

Now, verdict calibration. Let me enumerate findings:

**F1 — Title/description vs diff mismatch (the PR says "re-pin to fd84ab19", the diff pins `@main`).**
- The PR title: "chore(pin): awf workflows → fd84ab19". The diff contains no fd84ab19 anywhere; it introduces mutable `@main` tracking across all five reusable-workflow consumers.
- The commit on the branch documents "Owner directive 2026-10-04: consumers follow awf main" — so the diff is likely the intended state and the title/description are stale.
- Why blocking: what a reviewer approves must be what merges. The description promises an immutable-SHA bump (auditable, reversible); the diff delivers a supply-chain posture change (every awf push to main — reviewed PRs only, per the commit — live-runs in this repo with `actions: write`, `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write` permissions). Approval of the described change ≠ approval of the delivered change. Per verdict rules, scope violation = BLOCKING.
- Remedy: retitle/redescribe the PR to "track @main per owner directive" (or, if fd84ab19 was truly wanted, fix the diff). Also update stale comments (F2) in the same pass.

Hmm — wait. Let me think again about whether F1 is truly BLOCKING vs IMPORTANT. The verdict rules: "🚨 BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss."

- Scope violation: yes, literally — PR description and diff describe different changes. That's within the BLOCKING definition.
- Security issue: switching to @main tracking without an accurate description means the security-posture trade-off isn't actually surfaced for approval. The commit message does document it, but the PR (the reviewable unit) misrepresents it.

I'll go BLOCKING on the mismatch (fix = update title/description, a cheap but mandatory correction), and the mutable-pin supply-chain note rides along in that comment. Actually — let me be careful not to be pedantic-machine that blocks on a title. But no: in a machine-driven review loop, the PR description IS the contract the machine and reviewers act on; a reviewer/keeper validating "pin = fd84ab19" would verify the wrong thing.
